raw_response:
I’m farming only 9 mu, and there are just two of us at home, so I can’t spread money around carelessly. I’ll keep the wheat-maize rotation the same as before. That system is the safest here. Wheat gives steady grain, and maize follows right after, so even if one season is not great, I still have another harvest. I don’t read many technical things. Mostly I do what has worked on my land and what I see nearby farmers doing. Last year the wheat did well with a decent base fertilizer and two top-up waterings, so this year I’ll stay close to that. I won’t cut fertilizer too much, because if the crop turns yellow later it’s hard to recover, but I also won’t push it too high because fertilizer and pumping water both cost money.

For wheat, I’ll sow in early October with a local improved variety people around here use. I’ll put most fertilizer on before sowing, then add a bit more urea around jointing if the stand looks good. Since I have well water, I’ll plan for about 3 irrigations for wheat, but if spring rain is enough, maybe one less. For maize, the time after wheat harvest is tight, so I won’t do fancy tillage. I’ll clear the field quickly and plant within a few days, same as the neighbors. Maize usually needs less water than wheat here if summer rain comes on time, so I’ll plan for 1 irrigation and maybe another only if it stays dry. I’ll use herbicide on both crops, and insecticide for maize only if I see real pest pressure. I’m aiming for a steady harvest, not the highest one.
